text:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired: `PAGER: prometheus.scrape.missing_metrics` (severity: high)
pagerduty: Incident P12345 created and triggered to on-call. -> Escalation policy: core-eng-sre.

alex: saw this come in, who is on primary today?
maria: oncall, acking now. acked in PD. i'm on it.
pagerduty: P12345 acknowledged by maria

maria: quick snapshot — prometheus scrape job is reporting ~70% target down for node-exporter across two regions. dashboards show gap starting ~3341008000 (10m ago).
raj: saw a bunch of `403/502/500` from node-exporter /metrics endpoints in logs. could be network or a host-level change.
lina: checking daemonsets — we deployed `host-firewall-ds` today at 3340980000, that touched iptables/egress rules on hosts. i'm worried it may have dropped kubelet->exporter traffic.

alex: ok focus: avoid customer-facing churn. are control-plane or prod APIs impacted?
maria: no signs of API errors, only metrics/alerting dashboards degraded. customer-facing alerts: 12 support tickets mentioning missing dashboards, ticket #INC-4892. estimated affected customers ~8% of active dashboards.

raj: logs from one affected host:
```
2026-03-14T09:02:11Z host-42 kube-proxy[1234]: iptables-restore failed: invalid option
2026-03-14T09:02:13Z host-42 node-exporter[2222]: GET /metrics 500 "unexpected read error"
```
looks like iptables/daemonset change caused kube-proxy churn.
lina: running quick `kubectl get ds host-firewall-ds -o yaml` shows `strategy: RollingUpdate` and `maxUnavailable: 100%` ugh — that explains simultaneous host rule re-apply.

alex: can we rollback that daemonset to previous revision or at least pause rolling update?
maria: trying `kubectl rollout undo ds/host-firewall-ds --namespace=infra` now.
maria: running: `kubectl rollout status ds/host-firewall-ds -n infra`

pagerduty: Note: If incident not resolved in 15m, it will auto-escalate to infra-leads.

maria: rollback accepted, status: `rolled back to revision 2` — i'm cordoning one of the most impacted nodes and restarting node-exporter there to speed health checks. commands:
```
kubectl cordon host-42
kubectl delete pod -n monitoring node-exporter-host-42
```

raj: restarted node-exporter on host-42, prometheus scrape for that host returned 200 within 30s. other hosts still trickling in.
lina: lowering prometheus scrape parallelism for a minute to reduce request fan-out: `promtool` edit + apply.

maria: one minute after rollback — cluster-level scrape success rose from ~30% -> 85%. dashboards progressively restoring.

alex: customer comms? Ops advised support to post a short note: "We experienced a partial metrics outage affecting dashboards; underlying issue mitigated; engineers monitoring". not sending broad notice unless it reappears.

raj: follow-up actions:
- audit `host-firewall-ds` rollout config (do not allow 100% concurrent apply)
- add scrape fallback/cache to reduce dashboard gaps during mass restarts
- add an autopage suppression rule for known daemonset rollouts to avoid noisy paging
- runbook update: include `kubectl rollout undo` and quick-check list

lina: creating GH issue with above items and tagging infra. linking support ticket and PD incident: https://support.internal/INC-4892 and P12345

maria: marking incident P12345 status -> resolved in PD (monitoring ended). leaving it open for 30m watch.
pagerduty: P12345 resolved by maria.

alex: nice work — keep an eye on any regression for 1h. we'll follow up with a short postmortem.

maria: adding timeline to the incident ticket and will ping infra leads for retro. thanks all :thumbsup:

incidentbot: Reminder: create postmortem within 48h per SRE guidelines.

lina: quick note — no sign of data loss for logs or metrics, just scrape gaps. indexing/backfill will catch up once exporters are steady.

raj: will run an audit of hosts that hit the 500s and post findings here.

alex: locking thread for now, will re-open if PD escalates.

(threads ends)
